messages.content: Include exactly 5 numbers in the response. For a generative AI system, suppose a generated output is substantially similar to an item in the training dataset. Does this prove that the training dataset item was memorized?

message.content: No. Substantial similarity does not prove memorization. The overlap can arise from at least 3 distinct causes: (1) the prompt itself constrains the output space so heavily that convergence is expected, (2) the model learned a general template or pattern that coincidentally mirrors a specific training example, and (3) the training item was not actually unique—public facts, common phrasings, or widely-circulated text appear in multiple sources. To argue memorization, researchers typically require the model to reproduce the text verbatim or near-verbatim (often measured by exact-token match rates) when given a distinctive or low-frequency input, and they compare against a held-out test set of 100+ items to rule out chance. Similarity alone, without such controls, is inconclusive evidence.
